content.text:
I've submitted index 6 (Sb fraction 0.255) as the best composition. The evidence behind it is weak: it had the highest EQE of the five I measured, but only 0.040%, and the noise is about as large as the values themselves.

All 5 EQE measurements are used; I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | 0.255 | 0.040 |
| 17 | 0.59 | 0.022 |
| 19 | 0.65 | 0.018 |
| 21 | 0.71 | 0.011 |
| 13 | 0.45 | −0.041 |

- **Noise:** index 13 gave a negative reading, which is physically meaningless for a photoanode and suggests the noise is around ±0.04%. So index 6 may not really beat index 17.
- **Uneven sampling:** I spent four measurements on the Sb-rich side, near CrSbO4 (Sb 0.5), because I expected the peak there. All of those readings were low. Index 6 was my only point on the Cr-rich side. The full Cr-rich range, Sb 0.14–0.35, is barely explored, so the true best composition on the line could be there and unmeasured.
- **Gaussian-process tool:** after three measurements it gave no useful guidance, just a flat prediction near zero with the same uncertainty everywhere.

If you run this line again, I'd sample the Cr-rich range more densely and use XRD to check which phases are present before spending EQE measurements.
